scraped_articles.title: CBI arrests SFIO official and two others in alleged ₹1 crore graft case
scraped_articles.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a Deputy Director-level official of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) and two others, including an advocate, in an alleged corruption case.
The accused persons have been identified as Harish Kumar Tanwar, an investigating officer posted with the SFIO office in Chennai; advocate Bharat Sharma; and his relative, Aryan Sharma. Mr Tanwar is an Indian Revenue Service official (Income Tax) of 2007 batch.
The CBI registered the allegations that the accused official and others had demanded ₹1 crore from the complainant for favouring him in an investigation being conducted by the SFIO related to “DHFL scam”.
After verification of the complaint and registration of the First Information Report, the CBI laid a trap. The three accused were arrested after the advocate allegedly received ₹20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe of ₹1 crore, for and on behalf of the SFIO official, the agency said.
Published- October 15, 2026 02:09 pm IST

scraped_articles.title: Ankita Bhandari murder: Parents released after detention, issue ultimatum to government
scraped_articles.content:
Parents of 19-year-old Ankita Bhandari, who was murdered in Uttarakhand in 2022, were released early on Thursday (October 15, 2026) morning, hours after being detained while protesting near India Gate against Dushyant Kumar Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim Governor.
During the detention, her father issued a 24-hour ultimatum to the Centre to cancel Mr. Gautam’s appointment.
Police detained the parents during the protest and released them around 5 a.m., sources said.
Ankita’s father threatened to launch a nationwide agitation if the government did not accept their demand. Her family has been alleging that Mr. Gautam played a key role in Ankita’s death.
“We give a 24-hour ultimatum to the government for the cancellation of Dushyant’s appointment. Nationwide protests will be launched if the government does not accept our demand,” Ankita’s father toldPTIVideos.
Apart from the parents, several Congress leaders, including the party’s media and publicity department head Pawan Khera, social media department head Supritya Shrinate, and Indian Youth Congress chief Uday Bhanu Chib, were also detained and later released.
The parents have been demanding that Dushyant Kumar Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim Governor be put on hold until the ongoing CBI investigation into the case is complete.
BJP leader Gautam’s name has been repeatedly dragged into the case by Ankita’s family and activists as the alleged VIP linked to it. He was appointed the Governor of Sikkim on Monday (October 12).
Ankita, who worked as a receptionist at the Vanantra Resort in Rishikesh, was killed on September 18, 2022.
Her body was recovered from the Chilla canal four days later. Resort owner Pulkit Arya, son of former BJP leader Vinod Arya, and two accomplices have been convicted in the case and sentenced to life imprisonment.
The case hogged the political spotlight over allegations that an unidentified VIP was linked to the crime. Ankita’s family and activists have demanded an investigation into the alleged VIP angle, with Mr.Gautam’s name being raised in connection with the allegations.
Mr. Gautam has denied the accusations and initiated defamation proceedings against them.
The Congress has claimed that the appointment was aimed at shielding Mr. Gautam, arguing that a Governor cannot be subjected to criminal proceedings while holding office.
A former national general secretary of the BJP, Mr. Gautam had served as the party’s in-charge for Uttarakhand.
Published- October 15, 2026 07:58 am IST

scraped_articles.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested the executive director of Munition India Limited (MIL), a public sector defence enterprise, and two private persons in an alleged bribery case.
Besides the official, Anil Kumar, the CBI arrested his brother, ⁠B. Harshavardhan, and Ashish Kansal, the chief executive and director-promoter of SMPP Ltd.
Private industries in defence sector have big potential: official
The CBI registered the case against Mr. Kumar on Monday following allegations that he connived with private parties and demanded and accepted illegal gratification for extending official favours while being posted at MIL in Pune.
“During searches conducted on the premises of the accused public servant in Pune, ₹1.73 crore in cash was recovered. Further, searches on the premises of the accused at Mysuru, Bengaluru, and Delhi were conducted and about ₹50 lakh in cash and incriminating documents were recovered,” the CBI said.

scraped_articles.title: ’Blue drum’ murder case: Meerut court sentences wife, partner to death
scraped_articles.content:
New Delhi
A Meerut court on Wednesday sentenced Muskan Rastogi and her partner, Sahil Shukla, to death for murdering her husband, Saurabh Rajput, whose dismembered remains were found in a cement-filled plastic drum in March 2025.
Saurabh, a merchant navy officer, was killed on March 3 last year, and the body was discovered two weeks later.
District and Sessions Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra pronounced the sentence after convicting the duo of murder and destruction of evidence.
The case, which drew widespread attention because of the brutality of the crime, saw more than 100 hearings and the examination of 22 prosecution witnesses.
Prosecution lawyer K.K. Chaubey told reporters that the judge referred to theMahabharatawhile explaining the punishment, observing that “justice required punishment proportionate to the gravity of the offence”.
“Apart from the death sentence, the court also imposed fines totalling ₹70,000 on each convict for murder and the offence related to the disappearance of evidence,” Mr. Chaubey said.
The two accused, who attended the proceedings via video conference, reportedly broke down after the verdict was announced. Lawyers present in the courtroom distributed sweets following the pronouncement. The detailed court order is awaited.The crimeSaurabh, 35, returned to Meerut from London in late February 2025. According to the police investigation, when his family failed to trace him for several days, they approached the police, who recovered his dismembered remains from a cement-filled drum at the house he shared with Muskan. The couple’s six-year-old daughter allegedly pointed to the container when asked about her father’s whereabouts.
In the chargesheet filed in May 2025, the police claimed that Muskan and Sahil drugged Saurabh before stabbing him to death and dismembering his body. They allegedly placed his remains in the drum, sealed it with cement and sand, and left for a vacation in Himachal Pradesh. The police used industrial equipment to break through the hardened cement and retrieve the remains.
The police filed a nearly 1,000-page chargesheet detailing the evidence against the duo, including forensic reports, call records, CCTV footage and witness statements. Muskan, who was pregnant at the time of the crime, later gave birth to a girl while in jail.
Published- October 15, 2026 01:38 am IST

scraped_articles.title: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence seizes ₹30 crore worth of salt smuggled from Pakistan
scraped_articles.content:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) said it has detected and stopped another attempt by smugglers to bring into India goods from Pakistan, something that is prohibited, and has arrested four people related to the matter. In a release, the DRI said that it had detected the import of 295 containers carrying 7,311 metric tonnes of Pakistan-origin industrial or Himalayan rock salt, which it said had an estimated market value of around ₹30 crore.
Following thePahalgam terror attack in April 2025, the Indian government had banned the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, in the interest of national security and public policy.
It explained that the consignments were routed through Colombo Port in Sri Lanka, and had fake certificates of origin and invoices issued by UAE-based entities.
“Acting on specific intelligence, DRI launched a coordinated, fortnight-long operation between September 26 and October 11, 2026, conducting searches at linked premises in Gandhidham, Adipur, Veraval, Panipat, Pune, Patiala, Delhi and Mumbai,” the DRI said.
The investigation revealed that nine importers had brought in the 295 containers through Mundra and Kandla ports since March 2026, in violation of the prohibition on the import of goods originating in or exported from Pakistan.
Of the 295 containers detected, five containers carrying 140 MT of the salt, valued at ₹24.41 lakh, were seized at Kandla Port. Further, the proceeds of sales of this salt, amounting to ₹20.96 lakh, has also been seized from the importers’ bank accounts.
“Preliminary investigation has uncovered a transnational network involving entities owned by Pakistani, UAE, Sri Lankan and Indian nationals,” DRI said. “The network allegedly coordinated the shipments and supporting documentation to disguise the Pakistani origin of the goods.”
“Significantly, Bills of Lading relating to the Pakistan-Sri Lanka leg of the shipments and customs declarations filed with Sri Lanka Customs expressly mentioned Pakistan as the country of origin and India as the final destination,” it added. “The Certificates of Origin submitted by the importers were found to be fabricated.”
Two proprietors or partners of importing firms, a Customs broker’s G-card holder, and the owner of a Dubai-based supplier who had also established and operated an importing firm in his father’s name have all been arrested.

scraped_articles.title: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi meet murdered Ankita Bhandari’s parents as they protest Sikkim Governor appointment
scraped_articles.content:
The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and his sister, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) met the parents of the late Ankita Bhandari, who were staging a sit-in protest near India Gate against the appointment of Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Governor of Sikkim.
Also Read:The murder that shook a mountain
Bhandari, who had worked as a receptionist at the Vanantra Resort in Uttarakhand’s Pauri district, was killed in 2022 by her employer, Pulkit Arya, the son of a BJP leader, and two of his aides. The investigation found that she was murdered after refusing to provide “special services” to a VIP who was scheduled to visit the resort in the week of her death.
In August 2025, after nearly three years of trial, a sessions court sentenced the three accused to life imprisonment.
Despite the convictions, Bhandari’s family and supporters have continued to demand a thorough investigation into the alleged VIP angle in the case. Her parents alleged that Mr. Gautam, a former Rajya Sabha MP and BJP general secretary was the VIP in question. They held that his political influence had prevented his name from being included in the investigation.
Mr. Gautam has categorically denied all these charges and even filed a defamation suit in the Delhi High Court earlier this year against several people, including the Uttarakhand Congress party.
Speaking to the media at India Gate, Bhandari’s parents, Virendra Singh Bhandari and Soni Devi, urged President Droupadi Murmu to suspend Mr. Gautam’s appointment until the ongoing Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the alleged VIP connection in their daughter’s murder is completed.
Mr. Gandhi had met the family in August and expressed concern that they were still waiting for answers years after their daughter’s death.
“For four years, Ankita Bhandari’s family has not received justice, but a ‘VIP’ accused has certainly been rewarded with protection and a constitutional position,” he wrote on X after meeting Mr. Bhandari.
He added: “Where rapists and murderers are welcomed with garlands and criminals are honoured with positions of authority, no hope can be expected from such a misogynistic BJP. Today, Ankita’s parents, carrying their plea for justice for their daughter, are sitting at India Gate, miles away from their home. I and the Congress Party stand with them in their grief as well as in this fight for justice.”
Amid the recent controversy, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Wednesday said that his government had ensured swift arrests, a SIT investigation, life imprisonment for the convicts, and even recommended a CBI investigation in the matter.
Published- October 14, 2026 09:30 pm IST

scraped_articles.title: Delhi HC calls for report from jail on non-appearance of Yasin Malik in terror case
scraped_articles.content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) called for a report from the jail authorities on the non-appearance of separatist leaderYasin Malikfrom prison in a terror funding case.
A Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj noted that Mr. Malik was to be produced before the court virtually.
“Respondent (Malik) had to be produced virtually before us. However, it is not done. Let a report in this regard be called from the jail superintendent concerned,” the Bench said.
The Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front chief (JKLF) chairman is lodged in Tihar jail where he is serving a life term in the case.
The court listed the matter for further hearing on December 9 and directed that on that day, Mr. Malik be made to join the proceedings virtually.
The court was hearing a plea by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) seeking death penalty for Mr. Malik in the terror funding case.
Mr. Malik had earlier said he wishes to argue in-person against the NIA’s plea seeking enhancement of his punishment from life term to death penalty.
On May 29, 2023, the high court issued notice to Mr. Malik on the NIA’s plea and sought his presence before it on the next date.
Subsequently, jail authorities filed an application seeking permission for his virtual appearance on grounds that he was a “very high-risk prisoner” and it was imperative to not physically produce him in court to maintain public order and safety.
The request was allowed by the high court.
Published- October 14, 2026 05:46 pm IST

scraped_articles.title: Punjab police arrests key operative in social media influencer Mad Sandhu murder case
scraped_articles.content:
The PunjabPolice on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) said they have apprehended a key operative, identified as Jobanpreet Singh, in the murder of social media influencer Mad Sandhu, fromMumbai
Director General of Police (DGP) Gaurav Yadav on Wednesday (October 14) said that Counter Intelligence (CI) Jalandhar, in coordination with the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) apprehended Jobanpreet Singh from Chembur in Mumbai.
“The arrested accused, Jobanpreet Singh is a resident of village Jandoke in district Tarn Taran. Police teams have recovered three sophisticated pistols—including one 9MM Glock, one 9MM Beretta and one .30 bore PX5—along with five magazines and 11 live cartridges from his possession,” he said.
On October 3, 2026, two motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at Madhu Sudan Singh alias Mad Sandhu on Loharka Road in Amritsar, resulting in his death. An FIR under sections 103 and 3(5) of theBharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)and sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act was registered at Police Station Cantonment at Commissionerate Amritsar.
Earlier, two of his module associates, identified as Harsimranjit Singh alias Sangha and Fateh Singh, both residents of Village Sanghe, Tarn Taran, were also tracked down and apprehended in Surat, Gujarat, in a coordinated operation with Gujarat ATS. A total of 11 persons, including one of the shooters, have been arrested in this case.
“Preliminary investigation has established that Jobanpreet Singh played a pivotal role in arranging weapons, financing, and providing logistical support to the shooters at the behest of foreign-based handlers. During interrogation, accused Jobanpreet confessed to his involvement in three separate extortion-linked firing incidents in Tarn Taran district. Further investigation is underway to uncover the wider network and establish its backward and forward linkages, he added.

scraped_articles.title: Supreme Court makes protection from arrest ‘absolute’ for journalist who reported on Ayodhya Temple theft allegations
scraped_articles.content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) made absolute the interim protection granted to independent journalist Abhishek Upadhyay from coercive action in a road rage case, as well as any subsequent First Information Reports.
Mr. Upadhyay had authored investigative online stories of the alleged misappropriation and theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple.
A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi also quashed an Uttar Pradesh Police notice issued to social media platform X to provide Mr. Upadhyay’s digital data, generated around three months prior to the road rage incident.
The court found the police version that the data was sought to trace/arrest the petitioner “somewhat in contradiction” with the contents of its notice to the platform.
The court termed the notice an “overkill”, and said any information received by the police pursuant to the notice would not be used against the journalist.
The “arrest of the petitioner (Mr. Upadhyay) shall remain stayed till further notice,” the court said. It made absolute its interim orders of August 25 and September 7, which had protected him from arrest and directed him to cooperate with the investigation, respectively.
The copy of the road rage FIR had been supplied to the petitioner, the court noted.
The Bench ordered that Mr. Upadhyay could challenge the road rage FIR on any grounds. The apex court has not commented on the merits of the case.
The court allowed Mr. Upadhyay, who said the road rage case was “staged”, to counter his online reports about the temple, and the liberty to file a separate petition seeking guidelines to protect digital privacy and journalistic freedoms.
The apex court further directed the police to release the journalist’s vehicle in the next two days.

scraped_articles.title: CBI files supplementary chargesheet in NEET paper leak case
scraped_articles.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) filed a supplementary chargesheet against an accused in theNEET paper leak casebefore a Delhi court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026).
Special Judge Ajay Gupta directed that a copy of the supplementary chargesheet be supplied to the counsel of the 14th accused, Sheshrav Bajrang Suryawanshi, alias Raj Suryawanshi, and posted the matter for further proceedings on Thursday (October 15, 2026).
The agency has alleged that Mr. Suryawanshi, a resident of Nanded in Maharashtra who was arrested on September 2, 2026, is a close associate of co-accused Shubham Khairnar.
According to the supplementary chargesheet, Mr. Suryawanshi, acting in collusion with Mr. Khairnar, provided the medical entrance examination paper to various candidates and collected money from their families.
CBI officials said Mr. Suryawanshi allegedly asked the candidates to gather at a place in Nanded, where they were provided with the paper. He kept their original documents, such as educational certificates and identity cards, to ensure that they made the payment after the examination.
On August 12, 2026, the designated fast-track court dealing with “criminal cases arising from paper leaks as well as the use of other unfair means in public examinations” took cognisance of the CBI’s chargesheet against 13 other accused.
According to the earlier chargesheet, the agency began its crackdown on May 13, 2026, with the first set of arrests of Mangilal, Dinesh and Vikas Biwal in Rajasthan. Their mobile phones contained leaked PDFs received via Telegram on April 29, 2026.
On the same day, the agency arrested Yash Yadav in Gurugram and Mr. Khairnar in Nashik.
Another key arrest made on May 13, 2026, was that of Dhananjay Lokhande in Pune. He allegedly attempted to destroy his phone to clear evidence before being apprehended.
Manisha Sanjay Waghmare was arrested in Pune the next day. According to the final report filed earlier, Ms. Waghmare was “one of the prime conspirators in the leakage and dissemination of NEET-UG 2026 questions for monetary consideration” and “acted as the link between candidates and the subject experts.”
After interrogating them, the agency arrested the alleged mastermind, P.V. Kulkarni, from Latur on May 15, 2026, followed by Manisha Mandhare from Pune on May 16, 2026.
Shivraj Motegaonkar, the founder of a coaching centre in Latur, was picked up on May 17, 2026.
The last arrests in this case were of Manisha Sanjay Havaldar from Latur on May 22, 2026, and Tejas Shah and Dr. Manoj Shirure, both from Latur, on May 26, 2026.
The CBI has claimed that the conspiracy was unearthed through forensic imaging of mobile devices, which recovered deleted WhatsApp chats and PDF documents containing the leaked questions.
The National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or NEET-UG, is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for admissions to medical courses.
On May 12, 2026, the NTA cancelled the exam held on May 3, 2026, amid paper leak allegations. A re-examination was conducted on June 21, 2026.
The NEET paper leak snowballed into a major political issue, triggering a massive protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The protest culminated in theresignation of Dharmendra Pradhanas Union Education Minister.
The CBI swung into action after registering the FIR, raiding 92 locations in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi and other States.
During its two-month-long probe, the agency unearthed the conspiracy from the source of the leak to the beneficiary candidates, leading to the “identification of the chain.”
